summary: Sprint 2 — Production Engine — fully verified. Full pytest suite (77/77 tests, 44.17s) is GREEN across 13 files, including the 16 new production-engine tests. All 20 acceptance items in the review request are satisfied: (1) seeded system ProductionUnitType rows (HATCHERY_TANK, NURSERY_TANK, GROW_OUT_POND, CAGE, RACEWAY, BIOFLOC_TANK) with is_system=true; (2) auto-created default Main Site on farm creation (code=MAIN, is_default=true); (3) site soft-delete guardrail returns 409 with 'active production unit' when units exist and succeeds after unit deletion; (4) site restore endpoint re-enables soft-deleted sites; (5) custom ProductionUnitType lifecycle honors 409-on-system-code-clash, 403-on-system-delete, and 200-on-own-custom-delete; (6) ProductionUnit lifecycle blocks delete on active batch (409 with 'active batch'); (7) batch full lifecycle PLANNED→STOCKED→ACTIVE→HARVESTED→CLOSED works via events + explicit transitions with stocked_at/harvested_at/closed_at populated; (8) terminal CLOSED state blocks new events (409); (9) invalid transitions return 409 with correct hints ('Invalid batch transition', 'stocking event'); (10) transition history includes the initial (null→planned) row; (11) concurrent transitions to different targets yield exactly one 200 and one 409 via CAS primitive; (12) GET /api/v1/production-events/catalog returns all 9 event types with code/display_name/category/version/triggers_transition_to/schema/metadata; (13) event catalog rejects unknown event_type (400 with 'unknown event_type'), extra fields (422 with field 'totally_extra'), and missing required (422 with field 'quantity'); (14) cursor pagination is disjoint across pages with (performed_at DESC, id DESC) ordering; (15) cross-tenant access returns 404 for every read/list URL {site,unit,batch,batch/events,batch/transitions,events/{id}}; (16) all 7 Production Engine source files lint clean (models/schemas/repositories/services/endpoints/event_catalog/alembic migration); (17) FastAPI app boots (backend supervisor RUNNING); /health returns 200 with rate_limiter block ({"status":"ok","rate_limiter":{"healthy":true,"backend":"in-memory"}}); (18) OpenAPI enumerates 31 Production Engine routes under /api/v1/* including /production-events/catalog, /production-unit-types, /organizations/{id}/production-unit-types, /farms/{id}/sites, /sites/{id}(+/restore,/units), /units/{id}(+/batches), /batches/{id}(+/transitions,/events), /events/{id}.
critical_code_review_comments: endpoints/production.py list_unit_types / list_events use `= None  # type: ignore` fallback for Annotated Depends parameters after non-default params (organization_id / event_type). This works because FastAPI resolves Depends before signature defaults, but is fragile: a linter upgrade or a re-order could break it. Consider promoting the Query params to keyword-only or making them Optional with an explicit default of Query(None) before the Depends param.

endpoints/production.py:172 _load_site_and_farm imports FarmRepository/OrganizationMembershipRepository/FarmMembershipRepository/RoleAssignmentRepository + get_current_farm INSIDE the function body on every call. Hot path (every site/unit/batch/event endpoint hits this at least once). Move imports to module top-level unless there is a real circular-import reason — a comment explaining the local import would help future refactors.

endpoints/production.py:378-397 delete_site and delete_unit routes return the ProductionSitePublic/ProductionUnitPublic body but the resource was just soft-deleted; consumers might reasonably expect 204 or a body containing deleted_at. Either doc the choice on the endpoint's description or return the updated model with deleted_at populated so clients can render 'deleted at ...'.

endpoints/production.py:463-480 PATCH /batches/{id} applies `changed = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` then setattr's arbitrary fields. If the ProductionBatchUpdate Pydantic schema ever gets a `state` field (e.g. someone adds it in a future PR), the state-machine invariant would silently break. Recommend adding an explicit assertion / defensive filter that rejects 'state' at the endpoint boundary even if the schema is misconfigured (defence-in-depth against the very invariant this sprint enforces). Same concern applies to PATCH /sites/{id} and PATCH /units/{id} for tenancy-critical fields like farm_id/site_id.

endpoints/production.py:527-531 get_event_catalog is authenticated (uses `user: CurrentUser`) but the docstring in the router header (line 21) says 'public — reference data'. Reconcile the docstring with the implementation — either drop the CurrentUser dep or fix the comment; the implementation is currently the safer choice.

event_catalog.py:83 TransferEventSchema.destination_batch_id is typed `str = Field(min_length=1, description='UUID of the target batch.')`. Description says UUID but there is no UUID format validation. Consider `uuid.UUID` type or a Field(pattern=uuid_regex) so the catalog rejects non-UUID strings up front.

event_catalog.py:87 HarvestEventSchema.is_final=True is what triggers the HARVESTED transition, but this coupling is entirely inside services/production.py — the CATALOG registration for HARVEST has triggers_transition_to='harvested'. The catalog therefore advertises an unconditional harvest→harvested, which is only accurate when is_final=True. Two options: (a) add metadata={'transition_conditional_on': 'is_final==true'} so the frontend can render the correct UX, or (b) split HARVEST into HARVEST_PARTIAL and HARVEST_FINAL. Current behavior is correct but under-documented.

production/event_catalog.py __all__ (line 203) exports `datetime` and `ValidationError`. Neither is defined nor used at module level — `datetime` is imported but unused (line 27) and `ValidationError` is re-exported from pydantic. Small hygiene: remove the unused imports or add a `# re-export` comment; ruff/pylint will flag the unused datetime import once F401 is enabled on this file.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Sprint 2 (Production Engine) is fully accepted. All 77 pytest cases pass in ~44s. Canonical FastAPI backend lives at /app/apps/api; the pod shim at /app/backend/server.py (port 8001) does NOT include production routes and only exposes /health, /version, /api/v1/auth/*, /api/v1/health/*, /api/v1/version/* — this is expected per the problem statement ('The pod shim at /app/backend/server.py is unchanged'). Do NOT curl the shim to validate production endpoints; use pytest AsyncClient or `python -c 'from app.main import create_app; app = create_app(); ...'` against /app/apps/api. The state-machine invariant 'state changes ONLY via /transitions or via events that trigger transitions' is enforced in services/production.py — the PATCH /batches/{id} endpoint currently trusts that ProductionBatchUpdate has no state field; if that schema is expanded, add a defensive filter (see critical_code_review_comments). The concurrent-transition test asserts sorted statuses == [200, 409], which the CAS primitive in ProductionBatchRepository.compare_and_set_state guarantees — do not modify.
